deviations: Only the needed columns of the PISA files were read (data.table::fread select=); the replicate weights and other variables were skipped.

Table 1 (cols 1, 2, 3, 5) is estimated on an evenly spread block sample (about 20% of the rows, 0.5 MB blocks visited in van der Corput order until a 228 s time budget ran out) of Replication/Data/CSV/pisa_full_gps_final.csv. The full 3 GB file cannot be read through the read-only mount within the 300 s sandbox limit (measured raw throughput about 5-8 MB/s). All 49 countries and 253 of 263 country-waves are in the sample. Within each country-wave the sampled students' wgtc weights are rescaled to that cell's full weight (1/#waves of the country), keeping equal weight per country. The sample is timing-dependent, so a rerun can draw a slightly different subset.

table1_col3_observations is the observation count read from the <N> tag of the pisa_full_gps_final.dta header (1,992,276) times the complete-case share in the block sample (1.0); it is not the N of the sample regression. It is printed with %.6g as 1.99228e+06.

The preference measures are used as supplied in the data files (patience, risktaking, coo_* variables). These appear to be GPS measures z-standardised at the individual level in the analytical sample and then collapsed to the country level. They were not re-standardised across students.

Table 2 weights are the supplied student weight wgt (sampling weights normalised per residence country-wave), unchanged. Singletons are kept (fixef.rm='none'), so N = 80,398. Table 2 SEs are clustered by country of origin, Table 1 SEs by country.
notes: Table 1: weighted least squares of pv1math (PISA math / 100) on country patience and/or risk-taking with controls female, age, migration status (migra1, migra2), imputation dummies (imfemale, image, immigra0-2) and wave fixed effects. Weights are wgtc (equal weight per country); SEs are clustered by country. Natives (col 5) are students with migra1+migra2 < 1, and the migration dummies are dropped there. Table 2: migrant file pisa_full_gps_final_imcoo (80,398 students; 58 origin countries; 48 residence countries; 180 country-wave cells). Regressors are origin-country preferences plus female, age, OECD-origin dummy and imputation dummies, with residence country-by-wave fixed effects, wgt weights and SEs clustered by origin country. Claim attempt 1 (attempt-4) re-standardised the preferences across students and gave Table 2 equal weight per country; every coefficient was about 3x too small. Claim attempt 2 used the supplied variables and weights, and check_attempt then reported all claims within tolerance; that run is the final one, unchanged. Attempts 1-3 were exploratory (attempt 1 timed out while reading the full CSV; attempts 2-3 measured read speed and inspected variables).
